title: AI Creators: Build Real Things with AI
tagline: A year-long, hands-on course where middle schoolers learn HOW to use AI tools and WHY they work — and leave with a portfolio of images, videos, a website, an AI agent, an app and a game.
budget: Free tools first · up to ~$20/month for ONE teacher account used for demos

modules.title: Launch: How AI Works
modules.boss: Prompt Duel + signed AI Safety Pact

modules.title: AI Images
modules.boss: Brand Kit for a fictional company (logo, social post, poster, study aid)

modules.title: AI Video
modules.boss: 30–60 s ad or explainer with an honest AI disclosure

modules.title: Websites & E-commerce
modules.boss: Live landing page + mini online store for your brand

modules.title: AI Agents & Workflows
modules.boss: An automation/agent that solves a real class problem

modules.title: Mobile Apps
modules.boss: Personal app: tracker, diary, AI tutor or scheduler

modules.title: Games
modules.boss: Remix a classic, then design and ship your own game

progression.studentsCan: Explain in plain words how generative AI predicts, write a structured prompt, and follow the safety pact.
Produce single media pieces with intent: composition, style, hooks, pacing — and disclose AI use.
Combine assets into a structured product (page anatomy, user journey, calls to action).
Design systems that run steps for them: triggers, actions, tools, APIs, human checks.
Plan and vibe-code an app with screens, navigation, data and login; test and debug it.
Design interactive rule systems (loop, mechanics, feedback, balance), playtest, iterate and present.

lessonTemplate.purpose: Retrieval practice on last lesson's ideas + a hook. Gets brains on before screens open.
One big idea with a visual (dual coding) and a worked example. Short to protect working memory.
Students make something real (project-based learning) with a checklist and teacher circulating.
Team challenge that applies the idea under light pressure; earns house XP.
Gallery walk / peer feedback (peer teaching, elaboration).
2–3 quick questions: retrieval + self-explanation. You read them to plan next lesson.

safetyThreads.how: Every tool is tagged (school account OK / 13+ / 18+). 18+ tools and accounts students can't legally make are teacher-led demos only.
Never upload real photos of classmates, teachers or other people. We use ourselves only with consent rules, stock/public-domain images, or AI-made characters.
No real brand logos, celebrities or copied characters. Make original brands; credit sources; understand fair use basics.
Label AI-made content (#MadeWithAI). Ads must be honest — no fake reviews or fake testimonials.
Never share full names, school, address, passwords or API keys with AI or online. Use nicknames.
AI can be confidently wrong (hallucination). Every module has a 'Spot the AI mistake' activity.

ageRuleKey.meaning: Allowed for students of all ages when used through a school-managed account (e.g. Google Workspace for Education, Canva for Education).
Students 13+ may use their own account with parent/guardian permission. Under-13s: teacher-led demo.
Students must be 13 or older. Under-13s: teacher-led demo or the listed alternative.
No student accounts. Teacher drives it on the projector; students write the prompts.
Professional tool or paid account used only by the teacher.
